summary.text: Drew Wrigley is the Republican incumbent Attorney General of North Dakota. He was appointed in 2022 after the death of Wayne Stenehjem, was elected to a full term that year, and previously served as lieutenant governor and U.S. Attorney.

paragraphs.text: Wrigley was born in Bismarck and grew up in Fargo.
He graduated from the University of North Dakota in 1988, with honors in economics and philosophy, and earned a law degree from American University's Washington College of Law in 1991.
Wrigley began his legal career as an assistant district attorney in Philadelphia.
He served as U.S. Attorney for North Dakota from 2001 to 2009 and again after a 2019 nomination, and as lieutenant governor from December 2010 to December 2016.
In 2022, after the death of Attorney General Wayne Stenehjem, Gov. Doug Burgum appointed Wrigley to the office, and he was elected to a full term that year.
He said in February 2026 that he would run for reelection, and he lives in Bismarck.
